stemMd: According to the passage, if inertia were the whole explanation for the effect of automatic enrolment, workers who would have joined a scheme voluntarily would
instructionsMd: Answer on the basis of the passage only.

options.label: A
options.textMd: lower their contributions to the default rate

options.label: B
options.textMd: opt out of the scheme more often than other workers

options.label: C
options.textMd: take longer to begin contributing than before

options.label: D
options.textMd: contribute at the rate they would have chosen without automatic enrolment

explanationMd:
The third paragraph states the inertia prediction directly: "If inertia is the whole story, a default should change nothing for them: they would have signed up and chosen their own rate anyway, and automatic enrolment merely spares them a form."

So under inertia alone these workers keep the rate they would have chosen themselves.

**How to check.** The passage sets the two readings against each other on exactly this group. Lowering contributions to the default is the prediction of the OTHER reading, the advice reading, and it is the pattern the studies found — which is why the passage treats the evidence as favouring advice.

distractorRationale.a: This is what the ADVICE reading predicts, not the inertia reading. The passage uses the difference between the two predictions to decide between them.
distractorRationale.b: Opting out is not discussed for this group. Under inertia the passage says nothing changes for workers who would have joined anyway, so there is no reason they would leave more often.
distractorRationale.c: Automatic enrolment, if anything, removes a step, "merely spares them a form". Nothing suggests a delay for workers who intended to join.

accessibilityText: A question about the passage on automatic pension enrolment. It asks what workers who would have joined voluntarily would do if inertia were the whole explanation. The options are: contribute at the rate they would have chosen anyway; lower contributions to the default; opt out more often than others; take longer to begin contributing.

provenance.notes: Original item contrasting two hypotheses' predictions. The main distractor is the rival hypothesis's prediction.

independentSolve.workingNotes: Passage: if inertia is the whole story, a default should change nothing for always-joiners; they would have signed up and chosen their own rate anyway. D matches. A is the advice-reading prediction; B and C are not supported.

review.notes: Author checked that exactly one option is defensible. Awaiting blind independent solve. Options were reordered after review to remove answer-position bias; ids and labels were remapped with the key.
